doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Orchestral writing and Chris Brubeck
summary: They discuss who writes the orchestra charts, Chris Brubeck's early scoring, and Lamb's New Year's resolution to write for woodwind quintet.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And does Chris write those orchestra charts?
He does some of them, a lot of those are Dave’s and if they’re not Dave’s some of them are Dave’s brother Henry. Is it Henry?

I recall when I interviewed him I was enamored at the time — well when he first came up with his first orchestral piece, I think it was called “Elementals.” And he didn’t know what he was doing. He pretty much told me, he said, “I didn’t know how to score, I didn’t know ranges really well.” And I could almost picture some of the orchestral people going, “I can’t read this, who did this?”

Sure man, God. You know now so that’s my goal is I’ve been wanting to do it for a long time is to write orchestral music and woodwind quintets and things. So I just started studying that, it’s my New Year’s resolution this year and I’m going to write something for maybe woodwind quintet or string quartet. Probably not orchestra but that’s my ultimate goal. I’ve got so many ideas for that and Chris Brubeck is a really great orchestral writer and has been really supportive in that. So I’m really excited to get that happening. You know that’s my dream.

Yeah. You can learn a lot when someone finally goes to play it, just like observing and watching the players, like do they grimace or like okay how come they made a face at that thing. What is it about that, I’ll try not to do that.
That’s a good one. You know. Have you done that? Have you done orchestral?

Yeah I’ve done some orchestral pieces and quintets and that kind of thing. It’s tricky with Finale or whatever if you use that stuff too because you can put anything you want into Finale and it will play it back perfectly. But then you give it to a live person it could be a different story.
Right. The learning curve is going to be —
